summary:
### TL;DR
- No GitHub Changelog entries in this period. Both updates are documentation changes.
- **AI-powered PR scanning only covers PRs that target the default branch or a protected branch.** The docs for AI Scan and the AI applications detector now state this scope explicitly. PRs into other branches are not scanned. ([AI applications scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-applications-scanning-for-pull-requests), [AI-powered security detections](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-powered-security-detections))
- **The `issues` `status_changed` workflow trigger fires in more cases than previously described.** It now explicitly includes assigning an issue and changes to a linked pull request. ([Events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows))

### Action required
Nothing this time.

Two documentation clarifications are still worth checking against your own setup:
- **AI Scan coverage:** if you rely on it for PRs into feature, release, or integration branches that are not protected, those PRs get no AI Scan coverage. Protect those branches or cover them with another control. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-powered-security-detections))
- **`status_changed` workflows:** these may run more often than expected. Pull request activity can now trigger them indirectly. ([source](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows))

### Security improvements
- **AI Scan and the AI applications detector (public preview): scope clarified.**
  - Scans run when a PR targeting the default branch or a protected branch is created, and after each new push.
  - The docs link to protected branches and rulesets, which suggests branches protected through rulesets also count.
  - Existing exclusions still apply: PRs from forks and PRs created by Dependabot are not scanned.
  - Findings still cannot be used in rulesets to enforce merge requirements.
  - The AI applications detector looks for code patterns and data flows that could lead to indirect prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, or excessive agency.
  - Sources: [AI applications scanning for pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-applications-scanning-for-pull-requests), [AI-powered security detections](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-powered-security-detections), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/91e6a471fb3d7800fc069d1482ea95f20b6f77b3)

### Docs changes worth reading
- **Events that trigger workflows: issue `status_changed`.**
  - The trigger now explicitly runs on status changes caused by creating, closing, reopening, or assigning an issue.
  - It also runs on status changes caused by changes to a linked pull request.
  - The preview note now points to a webhook-specific preview notice.
  - A reusable note on status-change editor validation was removed from this section.
  - The guidance on matching a status by its ID (taken from the payload's `status` object) is unchanged.
  - **Security angle:** activity on a linked PR can now indirectly start these workflows. Avoid running untrusted input from `github.event` in them without validation.
  - Sources: [page](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/ec65af578012a5f0adfb47403b431c052b138a3d)
- **AI Scan pages:** both pages now state that scans are limited to the default branch and protected branches (details above). The provided diffs are truncated, so other edits to the limitations sections may not be visible here. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/91e6a471fb3d7800fc069d1482ea95f20b6f77b3))
